Sophie (sales): FYI merchant demo tomorrow 10am PT. They want streaming ingest with function/tool calls and SSO authz. Need a short fallback plan if we hit backpressure. Can eng help with an example?
Mike (eng-platform): Happy to help. Do they need exactly-once delivery or best-effort?
Sophie (sales): Best-effort is fine but they want predictable latency and an example of SDK retry/backoff + server-side fallback to shorter responses. Also want a quick note on authz (SAML + role mapping).
Andre (eng-runtime): For streaming backpressure we usually recommend small windowed batches + client-side concurrency limit. Example config in our JS SDK:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.streaming.call({
  model: 'redwood-large-v2',
  stream: true,
  maxInflight: 3, // client concurrency cap
  batchWindowMs: 30, // short batching to avoid latency spikes
});
```
Priya (solutions): Can we also show a server-side fallback rule? Like route to a smaller quantized variant when queue > X.
Andre (eng-runtime): Yes — routing policy can be simple: if queue_length > 20 or p95 latency > 800ms then route to `redwood-large-quant` or `redwood-medium`. Example policy snippet: `routeIf(queue_len>20, 'redwood-medium')`. We can send a 2-slide snippet for demo.
Mike (eng-platform): For authz: merchants will use SAML. We support role mapping to model-access groups. Short blurb: "SAML assertion -> map group to Redwood role -> scoped API key with model allowlist". I can draft the wording.
Sophie (sales): Awesome. Also pricing question: customer asked whether streaming tokens billed differently for fallback. Can you say if cost is per-token irrespective of model?
Andre (eng-runtime): Billing is per-token for hosted API; routing to smaller model reduces cost per-token and overall tokens emitted. Streaming itself doesn't change billing semantics, just throughput/latency.
Priya (solutions): I'll prepare a one-page cheat sheet: demo steps, SDK snippet, fallback policy, and authz paragraph. Can someone paste the exact SDK method names for Python too?
Mike (eng-platform): Python example quick:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))
resp = client.streaming.call(model='redwood-large-v2', stream=True, max_inflight=3)
for chunk in resp:
    handle(chunk)
```
Priya (solutions): Perfect. Any enterprise blockers? e.g., they asked about VPC/private deployment for PCI scope.
Sophie (sales): Yes flagged — merchant requires PCI-in-scope decision. They want an architecture note for private deployments and key management.
Andre (eng-runtime): Private deployment + customer-managed KMS is usual route. Note: on-prem package needs 8 GPUs for the workload they described. I'll confirm exact sizing but flagging now.
Mike (eng-platform): I'll add a line: "Dedicated (reserved) pools are recommended for steady throughput; Private for PCI + full network isolation."
Sophie (sales): Great. Can someone drop a short one-paragraph we can paste into the SOW and the demo slides? Low friction.
Priya (solutions): Draft for SOW: "Redwood will provide a streaming integration demo showing SDK-based ingest with client-side concurrency limits and auto-routing fallbacks to smaller model variants. For PCI-sensitive workloads we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and reserved capacity to meet latency SLOs." Feel free to tweak.
Sophie (sales): Perfect. @Mike @Andre — could you push the two code snippets + 2-slide fallback diagram to the google slides link before EOD? https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/EXAMPLE
Mike (eng-platform): On it.
Andre (eng-runtime): Will add the fallback diagram and routing rule examples.
